title: Functional Coverage Not 100% - Analysis and Strategy
source_notes: Inspect unhit bins and map each to a requirement. Determine whether reachable, stimulus missing, sampling wrong, or overconstrained. Add directed constraints/sequences for reachable gaps and justify exclusions. Do not change bins simply to obtain 100%.

title: Multi-Channel DUT with Credit-Based Flow Control
source_notes: Track credits per channel: decrement on sends and increment on releases. Assert no send without credit, no over-return. Exercise simultaneous send/release, imbalance, delayed returns, reset, and starvation.

title: Constrained-Random Verification - How It Works
source_notes: Describe legal input space with constraints, randomize reproducibly, drive transactions, check with assertions/reference models, and use coverage to find gaps and guide constraints. Directed tests address rare boundaries.

title: FP Multiplier ALU Verification Strategy
source_notes: Use a bit-accurate IEEE-754 reference. Cover normals, zeros, infinities, NaNs, subnormals, boundary exponents, rounding modes and ties, overflow/underflow, and exception flags.

title: FIFO Verification - What to Verify, How, Corner Cases
source_notes: Verify order, data integrity, capacity, empty/full flags, and reset. Exercise fill/drain, simultaneous push/pop, wraparound, bursts, overflow/underflow attempts. Use a queue reference model.

title: Systolic Array UVM Testbench - PE Level and Sub-System Level
source_notes: At PE level, verify MAC arithmetic, saturation, enable/reset, latency. At array level, model data movement, wavefront scheduling, accumulation, and boundaries. Test matrix dimensions, stalls, tiling, flush.

title: 512-bit Transaction Split-Reassemble Over 64-bit Link
source_notes: Eight 64-bit beats. Define beat/byte order, IDs, last indication, backpressure. Reassemble only accepted beats, detect missing/duplicate/out-of-order pieces, compare the full payload.

title: Out-of-Order Scoreboard - Track and Match with Associative Array
source_notes: Store expected transactions keyed by unique ID. On response, reject unknown IDs, compare, delete. Check ID reuse, duplicates, timeouts, reset, and leftovers. If multiple requests per ID are legal, use a queue per ID.

title: Debug Scoreboard Mismatch - Step-by-Step Approach
source_notes: Start at the first mismatch; confirm checker alignment, reference inputs, reset, acceptance events. Trace one transaction through driver, input monitor, DUT, output monitor, and model. Compare widths, signedness, masks, endian, latency, IDs. Classify DUT vs monitor vs model fault.

title: Router UVM Testbench - Complete Design
source_notes: Ingress agents and egress monitors, an independent route/arbitration model, packet reconstruction, and a scoreboard for delivery and data integrity. Check flow control, buffer limits, multicast/drop rules, fairness, errors, and reset.

title: req/ack Handshake Testbench with Latency Checking
source_notes: Generate requests, monitor requests and acks, measure latency. Check min/max latency, no extra ack, request stability, reset. Cover zero/min/max delay and back-to-back traffic.

title: Out-of-Order Packet Scoreboard with Reconstruction
source_notes: Collect fragments by packet ID and index, track a received bitmap, reconstruct once complete, then compare. Reject duplicates, invalid indices, unknown IDs, and late fragments.

title: Credit Release Handshake Checker with SVA
source_notes: Maintain a checker credit count updated by sends/releases and assert legal bounds. SVA can check stable release metadata during stalls and ack latency. A boolean assertion alone cannot catch excess credits without state.

title: Lane Redundancy Remapping - SV Constraint Generator
source_notes: Constrain logical-to-physical lane indices in range, exclude failed lanes, require distinct mappings, and obey adjacency rules. Check enough healthy lanes exist.

title: PHY Link Training - Delay Code Sweep with PRBS Error Injection
source_notes: Sweep delay codes, wait for settling, apply PRBS, count errors per window. Find the passing eye and choose the center. Inject errors to verify thresholds, retraining, and reporting.

title: 12-Channel 32-bit Coverage Strategy
source_notes: Cover each channel for valid transfers, data patterns, boundaries, stalls, errors. Cross channel with mode/status. Avoid crossing all 32-bit values; use walking ones/zeros and toggle coverage for bit-level exercise.

title: UVM Backdoor Access - HDL Path and Usage
source_notes: Configure valid HDL paths, then use RAL backdoor or uvm_hdl_read/deposit/force. Consider simulator optimization/access flags (+acc). Force persists until release; deposit does not.

title: Firmware Writes 1 to enable_reg but Device Does Not Start - Debug
source_notes: Confirm the write reached the correct address with correct byte enables. Trace bus completion, decode, register storage, clock/reset/power state, prerequisite configuration, and start-event generation. Check self-clearing/edge semantics.

title: DV Environment for Software-Programmed Threshold Transaction Limiter
source_notes: Monitor programming writes and transactions. Model threshold meaning, update timing, comparison, and counter reset. Check limits 0/1/max, threshold changes while active, exact crossing, backpressure, interrupts.

title: 128-bit Parallel Bus - Stuck-at Fault and Short Wire Test Patterns
source_notes: All-zero/all-one patterns for stuck-at faults. Walking-one and walking-zero patterns isolate lines and expose shorts. Unique per-wire temporal signatures can distinguish wires efficiently (log2 N patterns).

title: Using AI-Generated Code in Verification - Risks and Workflow
source_notes: Treat generated code as an untrusted draft: review against the spec, compile/lint, run edge cases, compare with an independent model. Do not use the same generated algorithm as both implementation and oracle.

title: Memory Debug - Frontdoor Write + Backdoor Peek to Find Swap Bug
source_notes: Write address-distinct patterns through the frontdoor, inspect physical locations via backdoor. Compare expected mapping to actual storage. Also read frontdoor because symmetric write/read swaps can cancel and hide a fault.

title: Memory Verification - Complete Strategy and UVM Environment
source_notes: Verify address/data integrity, masks, latency, collisions, initialization, ECC, reset. Use a sparse reference memory and monitor-driven checking. Apply address-distinct, walking-bit, checkerboard, random patterns plus concurrent accesses.

title: Streaming Log Analyzer
source_notes: Read line by line, parse recognized formats, maintain counts/state without loading the file. Track line numbers, distinguish malformed records. O(total input) time, memory proportional to retained state.

title: Cross-Array Two-Sum Index Pairs
source_notes: Hash values of the second array to lists of indices. For each a[i], look up target-a[i] and emit every (i,j). O(n+m+K) where K is the output size.

title: Reverse a 32-Bit Unsigned Integer
source_notes: Repeat 32 times: `out=(out<<1)|(x&1u); x>>=1;`. Reverses bit order. Use unsigned shifts. Test zero, all ones, each single bit.

title: Python: Extract error lines using regex
source_notes: Compile a regex for the severity format and iterate the file, emitting matching lines with line numbers. Avoid matching incidental words like 'error_count=0'.

title: C: Check if the N-th bit is 1
source_notes: For unsigned x and 0<=n<W: `((x>>n)&1u)!=0`. Validate n first; out-of-range shifts are undefined in C.

title: Algorithm: Find the Element That Appears Once (XOR Trick)
source_notes: XOR all elements when exactly one occurs once and others occur twice. Pairs cancel; O(n) time, O(1) space. Fails for arbitrary multiplicities.

title: C++ Algorithm: Count Pairs with Equal Digit Sum
source_notes: Compute each number's digit sum, keep counts by sum; when a number with sum s arrives, add count[s] to total then increment. O(n*d). Use a wide counter.

title: C++ Design: Container with ADD, EXISTS, GET_COUNT
source_notes: unordered_map value->count. ADD increments, EXISTS checks count>0, GET_COUNT uses find (avoid operator[] insertion). O(1) average.

title: C++ Algorithm: Array Pair Product Query with Point Update
source_notes: For sum of pairwise products in a range, store range sum S and square-sum Q in a segment tree; answer (S*S-Q)/2 with O(log n) updates/queries.

title: Reverse a Linked List
source_notes: prev=null, cur=head; loop: next=cur->next; cur->next=prev; prev=cur; cur=next. Return prev. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: C: memcpy Safety Issues and Best Practices
source_notes: memcpy requires valid nonoverlapping ranges; use memmove for overlap. Check capacity, length overflow, pointer validity. Don't memcpy non-trivially-copyable C++ objects.

title: Minimize Result by Adding Parentheses to Expression
source_notes: For A+B, enumerate every opening position in A and closing position in B; evaluate left*(inner_left+inner_right)*right (absent factors = 1), keep the minimum. O(|A|*|B|).

title: Robot Matrix Diagonal Traversal
source_notes: Iterate diagonal sum d=0..R+C-2, visit (r,c) with r+c=d in bounds, reversing direction on alternate diagonals for zigzag. O(R*C).

title: Online Interval Merge with Streaming Input
source_notes: Maintain disjoint sorted intervals in an ordered map. For new [L,R], find neighbors, merge all overlapping, erase them, insert merged. O(log m + k).

title: Count Digits 0, 2, 4 in Range [0, n]
source_notes: Digit DP with tight/started flags, or place-value counting per digit; zero needs special handling for leading zeros. O(log n).

title: Longest Contiguous Same-Character Substring
source_notes: Single scan tracking current run length and best run. Reset on change. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: Place Lamp to Illuminate Maximum Objects
source_notes: For points on a line and fixed-length coverage, sort positions and use two pointers for the largest window with span <= L. O(n log n).

title: Cyclic Shift Validation
source_notes: Equal-length strings are rotations iff s2 is a substring of s1+s1. Use KMP for O(n).

title: Memory Allocator Simulation
source_notes: Keep free intervals sorted by address, allocated blocks keyed by ID. Allocate with first/best fit plus alignment and split; free validates and coalesces neighbors. Handle exhaustion, double free.

title: Byte Stream Chunk Merging
source_notes: Represent chunks by offset+data; merge contiguous ranges, define overlap policy (must match / prefer / report conflict), preserve gaps.

title: Merge Intervals and Return All Unique Numbers
source_notes: Sort by start, merge overlaps, then enumerate integers in merged ranges. O(n log n + K).

title: Sliding Window Maximum Sum and Starting Index
source_notes: Sum the first k, then slide adding new and subtracting outgoing; track best sum and index. Initialize from a real window so all-negative arrays work. O(n).

title: Index of Second Smallest Element
source_notes: Track smallest and second-smallest with indices in one pass. Clarify whether duplicates count. O(n).

title: Tournament Elimination Bracket
source_notes: Single elimination with n players needs exactly n-1 matches. Use byes if n is not a power of two.

title: Move Zeros to End (LC 283)
source_notes: Write index compacts nonzeros in order, then fill the rest with zeros. Stable, O(n), O(1) space.

title: Array Deduplication - O(n^2) to O(n) Optimization
source_notes: Hash set of seen values, append first occurrences (order preserved). O(n) expected. For sorted input, two pointers with O(1) space.

title: Fibonacci: Recursive vs Iterative, Complexity, and Sequence Output
source_notes: Naive recursion is exponential O(phi^n) with O(n) depth; memoization O(n)/O(n); iterative two-variable O(n)/O(1).

title: Parse Mixed UVM/Custom Simulation Log File
source_notes: Stream the file and dispatch recognized UVM/custom patterns to dedicated parsers. Normalize severity, time, component, ID, message. Don't double-count the UVM report summary.

title: Check if a Number Is a Power of 2 (Bit Manipulation)
source_notes: `n != 0 && (n & (n-1)) == 0`. A power of two has exactly one set bit.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum with Subset Tracking (Kadane's)
source_notes: Track current sum/start; restart when extending is worse; update best and [start,end]. Initialize from the first element so all-negative input works. O(n).

title: Count Number of 1 Bits in Binary (Popcount)
source_notes: Repeat `n &= n-1; count++` until zero (Brian Kernighan). O(number of ones).

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence (LC 128)
source_notes: Put values in a hash set; start counting only from x where x-1 is absent; extend while successors exist. O(n).

title: Longest Substring Without Duplicates (C++)
source_notes: Sliding window with last-seen positions; on repeat inside window move left to last_seen+1; track max. O(n).

title: Elevator Cargo - Minimum Trips with Weight Limit
source_notes: If at most two items per trip: sort, two pointers pairing lightest with heaviest if they fit. Arbitrary items per trip is bin packing (NP-hard).

title: Python - Remove Vowels / Remove Consonants from String
source_notes: `''.join(c for c in s if c.lower() not in 'aeiou')`. When removing consonants, keep vowels plus non-letters if intended. O(n).

title: Sort Python Dictionary by Value; Regex Match Two Strings
source_notes: `sorted(d.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])`. Use re.search / re.match / re.fullmatch deliberately; plain equality uses ==.

title: Sort Log File by Age and Write to Output
source_notes: Parse age as a number, keep record and index, stable-sort by age, write output. Lexicographic sorting of ages gives wrong order.

title: Python - Find Unpaired Numbers in a List
source_notes: Use Counter and select values with odd counts (or count==1 if exactly one occurrence is required).

title: Find the 3rd Smallest Value in an Integer Stream
source_notes: Keep a max-heap of size three of the smallest values; replace top when a smaller value arrives. O(n log 3).

title: Stacked NMOS Current Mirror Analysis
source_notes: A cascode mirror keeps the output transistor's drain voltage steadier, increasing output resistance and current accuracy, at the cost of higher output compliance voltage. Check saturation of all devices.

title: CMOS Inverter Vin-Vout Transfer Curve, Cascaded Stages
source_notes: Output near VDD at low Vin, near ground at high Vin, with a high-gain transition where both devices conduct. Sizing shifts the switching threshold. Cascaded stages restore levels; odd count inverts.

title: NMOS Pass-Gate Chain with Threshold Compensation
source_notes: An NMOS passes a strong 0 but a weak 1 (VDD - Vt, worse with body effect). Transmission gates or boosted gates improve high-level transfer.

title: Ring Oscillator and Single Inverter Feedback
source_notes: Ring oscillator uses an odd number N of inverters; f ≈ 1/(2*N*t_pd). A single inverter with feedback tends to settle near its switching point rather than robustly oscillate.

title: Pulse Latch - Pulse Generator Circuit
source_notes: Combine clk with an inverted delayed clk to make a narrow pulse on the rising edge; the latch is transparent during that pulse. Pulse width must satisfy latch timing across PVT.

title: Logical Effort - FO3, Sizing, F=GH
source_notes: Stage delay d=g*h+p; path effort F=G*B*H. Optimal stage effort ≈ F^(1/N). FO3 means load is 3x the input capacitance.

title: Circuit Optimization Techniques
source_notes: Sizing, buffering, logic restructuring, reduced fanout, clock gating, voltage scaling, pipelining — trade delay vs power vs area.

title: Two-Stage Inverter VDDh->VDDl vs VDDl->VDDh
source_notes: Low-to-high crossing can leave the high-voltage PMOS partly on (static current, bad VIH); high-to-low can violate input limits. Use level shifters.

title: NAND2 Sizing from Corresponding Inverter
source_notes: Series NMOS each ~2x the inverter NMOS width; each parallel PMOS ~ same as the inverter PMOS.

title: Master-Slave DFF - Component Purpose and Removal Analysis
source_notes: Opposite-phase master and slave latches give edge-triggered behavior. Feedback retains state; removing isolation permits transparency/race-through.

title: tsu, tc2q Measurement in SPICE; tcq vs tdc Plot
source_notes: Sweep data-to-clock separation and record clk-to-Q; define setup/hold as where tcq degrades by a criterion (e.g. 10%). Near the aperture tcq rises sharply (metastability).

title: 6T SRAM Operation, SNM, and Sizing
source_notes: Two cross-coupled inverters plus two access transistors. Read: precharge bitlines, assert WL, sense. Pull-down > access for read stability; access > pull-up for writeability. SNM from butterfly curves.

title: ROM Types and Sense Amplifier; Timing Order
source_notes: Mask ROM, fuse/antifuse, EPROM/EEPROM/Flash. Sense amp resolves small bitline differences. Read: precharge, decode, activate, develop, sense, capture.

title: Electromigration - DC, AC, Iavg, Irms, Black's Equation
source_notes: Current-driven metal atom transport causing voids/shorts. Black's equation: MTTF = A*J^(-n)*exp(Ea/kT). Follow foundry avg/RMS/peak current limits.

title: RC Low-Pass Filter - Transfer Function and Cutoff Frequency
source_notes: H(jw)=1/(1+jwRC), fc=1/(2*pi*RC), -3dB at cutoff, -20dB/decade beyond, phase to -90°.

title: Emulation versus RTL Simulation and FPGA Prototyping
source_notes: RTL sim: best debug, slow. Emulation: synthesizable design on dedicated hardware, much faster, transactor-based. FPGA prototype: fastest, least visibility, more partitioning/timing effort.

title: Behavior Question: Describe Your Most Proud Project
source_notes: Template: 'I built [system] to solve [problem]. I owned [part]. The hardest issue was [challenge]; I chose [approach] because [tradeoff]. I verified it with [evidence]; the result was [measured outcome]. Next time I would improve [lesson].' Don't invent numbers or claim teammates' work.

title: Behavior Question: Describe an Interesting Bug You Encountered
source_notes: 'We saw [symptom] under [trigger]. I reproduced it with [test/seed], narrowed it to [component], found [root cause]. I fixed it, added [focused check], reran [regression]. Lesson: [prevention].' Show how evidence separated DUT vs monitor vs model.

title: Find the Lighter Stone Among 9 (Balance Scale)
source_notes: Split into three groups of three. Weigh two groups; the lighter one (or the unweighed one if balanced) has it. Then weigh one stone vs another from that group. Two weighings suffice.
